highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.156.0 improves rendering reliability, memory use, and platform support across managed and native workloads.
highlights_body: This unreleased work speeds up image and text processing, fixes front-buffered streams, synchronizes Android texture rendering, and updates the supported Apple deployment baselines.

bullets.lead: Front-buffered streams no longer retain data unnecessarily
bullets.detail: Releases retained stream data promptly so applications that read through front-buffered streams avoid avoidable memory growth.

bullets.lead: Android texture rendering follows display refresh
bullets.detail: Synchronizes texture rendering with the display refresh cycle for more reliable Android presentation.

bullets.lead: Linux HarfBuzz uses bundled symbols locally
bullets.detail: Binds HarfBuzz functions from the bundled native library on Linux, avoiding reliance on externally resolved symbols.

bullets.lead: Managed image pixel copies are more efficient
bullets.detail: Reduces overhead when copying image pixels through the managed API.
Pools UTF-32 encoding buffers and avoids native feature-string allocations during HarfBuzz shaping.
Raises the minimum supported deployment versions for Apple targets.

bullets.lead: WebGPU support is packaged with the native WebAssembly library
bullets.detail: Includes emdawnwebgpu's WebGPU implementation in libSkiaSharp.a for WebAssembly consumers.

contributor_summaries.VirgilMing: Improved Linux HarfBuzz native binding behavior and browser sample test reliability
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Packaged the WebGPU implementation into the WebAssembly native library
